chapter.title: OF OFFENCES RELATING TO COIN AND GOVERNMENT STAMPS

heading: Person employed in mint causing coin to be of different weight or composition from that fixed by law.
text: Whoever, being employed in any mint lawfully established in [2][India], does any act, or omits what he is legally bound to do, with the intention of causing any coin issued from that mint to be of a different weight or composition from the weight or composition fixed by law shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
status_note: The Act is repealed. Kept in India Code's 'Repeal Acts' collection; record title reads 'The Indian Penal Code, 45 of 1860 (Rep., Act 45 of 2023)' (read 2026-11-21)

amendment_history.by_ref_raw: A. O. 1948, the A. O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951
amendment_history.footnote_text: The words “British India” have successively been subs. by the A. O. 1948, the A. O. 1950 and Act 3 of 1951, s. 3 and the Sch., to read as above.
